posts.text:
Existing-home sales fell 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, NAR reported on November 12, 2026.

The median price was up 0.4 percent from a year earlier, to $416,700. But unsold inventory reached 1.59 million units, a 5.1-month supply, up from 4.7 months in September and 4.4 a year earlier. Median time on market was 35 days, up from 33 in September.

National figures may not match the collateral market. Lenders can check recent comparable sales and days on market near the property before setting exit and ARV assumptions.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Light graphic titled Home sales slowed to 3.75M as supply rose to 5.1 months. Bars show months of supply: 4.4 in October 2025, 4.7 in September 2026, 5.1 in October 2026. Cards: median price $416,700, up 0.4 percent; time on market 35 days.

sources.title: Existing-home sales decreased 5.5% in October
sources.quote: Existing-home sales decreased 5.5% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million in October. The median existing-home sales price increased 0.4% to $416,700. Total housing inventory was 1.59 million units, up 1.3% from September and 4.6% from October 2025. Unsold inventory represented a 5.1-month supply, up from 4.7 months in September and 4.4 months in October 2025. The median time on market was 35 days, up from 33 days in September and 34 days in October 2025.

sources.title: October existing home sales sink to 16-year low, rates only partly to blame
sources.quote: Existing-home sales decreased 5.5% month-over-month to a rate of 3.75 million. Median existing-home sale prices increased more modestly, only crawling up 0.4% year-over-year to $416,700.

posts.text:
The national Case-Shiller index rose 2.1 percent over the year to August 2026. Chicago rose 6.7 percent. Seattle fell 2.0 percent. That is an 8.7 point spread between two of the 20 cities.

Take a property worth $500,000 a year ago. At the Chicago rate it is about $533,500 now. At the national rate, $510,500. At the Seattle rate, $490,000.

A citywide index does not value one property. Lenders can still compare local trends with the national figure when reviewing collateral values and exit assumptions.

What does a lender need to know before saying yes or no to an inquiry?

The apply page in Vaulted asks optional questions a lender decides on. Who is applying, a person or an entity, and is there a guarantor? What is the property type and purpose? What are the purchase price, value today, value after repairs and repair budget? Close-by date and exit plan? How many deals in the last 3 years?

The answers appear on the inquiry card and in the lender email.

A deal can be easier to judge when the basics arrive with it.

posts.text:
Picture a hypothetical $175,000 rehab loan that closes. The borrower moves out, and the house sits empty during the work. Then a pipe bursts, and the damage is $43,750.

That is 25 percent of the loan balance. If the policy has a vacancy clause, as many homeowners policies do, the insurer may limit or exclude some losses once the property has been vacant for a stated number of consecutive days. Whether a renovation counts as vacant depends on the policy wording.

Lenders can ask for the policy's vacancy wording and whether an endorsement or other coverage fits the project.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Bar graphic: a $43,750 water damage claim is 25 percent of an illustrative $175,000 loan. Three cards: a hazard policy may limit or exclude some losses after a stated vacancy period; vandalism, glass and water damage are examples; renovation status depends on policy wording.

sources.title: Unoccupied and Vacant Home Insurance: What to Know
sources.quote: Many insurance companies will limit coverage for homes that aren't lived in after a certain amount of time, typically 30 or 60 consecutive days. A policy may not pay for damage from the following scenarios if your house is vacant for an extended period: Broken glass; Vandalism; Burst pipes or other water damage.

sources.title: Policy Definitions of Vacancy and Occupancy
sources.quote: It bears mention that some older forms use 30 days, so be sure to check your specific policy language. Therefore, a dwelling being renovated can be considered to be vacant.

posts.text:
A borrower asks for more time on a $460,000 loan and offers a 1 percent extension fee, $4,600. Before answering, a lender can review these items, in one sensible order:

1. Value. Current condition and an updated valuation.
2. Taxes and insurance. Evidence that both are current.
3. Payment history. Record of performance, plus any delays explained.
4. Exit plan. A named repayment source, remaining steps and a realistic schedule.
5. Fee. Last, because $4,600 does not fix weak answers to the first four.

Terms vary by lender.

A borrower uploads a document through Vaulted. How long does it stay?

Files sent through a document request are kept for one year after upload. A daily scheduled job then deletes them. If an account is closed, all of its uploaded files are deleted.

Accepted file types are PDF, JPEG, PNG, HEIC, DOCX and XLSX, up to 20 MB, checked by their contents.

For a lender, that is a retention clock to plan around. Files needed past one year can be saved elsewhere first. Record keeping rules vary by state and by lender.

posts.text:
The Census Bureau put the U.S. rental vacancy rate at 7.6 percent in the third quarter of 2026, up from 7.3 percent in the second quarter and 7.1 percent a year earlier.

Why it matters for DSCR: one lender source defines it as gross monthly rent divided by the monthly PITIA payment. Take illustrative rent of $2,000 against a $1,500 payment. That is 1.33. Cut rent by 7.6 percent, or $152 a month, and it is 1.23.

A national rate is not a local one. Lenders can test a deal at a market vacancy rate, not only at full rent.
posts.alt: Bar chart of the U.S. rental vacancy rate: 7.1 percent in Q3 2025, 7.3 percent in Q2 2026, 7.6 percent in Q3 2026. Below, an illustrative DSCR test: $2,000 rent over $1,500 PITIA is 1.33, and rent cut by 7.6 percent to $1,848 gives 1.23.

sources.quote: National vacancy rates in the third quarter 2026 were 7.6 percent for rental housing and 1.2 percent for homeowner housing. The rental vacancy rate was higher than the rate in the third quarter 2025 (7.1 percent) and higher than the rate in the second quarter 2026 (7.3 percent).

sources.quote: DSCR is calculated by dividing a property's gross monthly rental income by its monthly housing payment, known as PITIA.

sources.title: Guide to DSCR Ratio & PITIA in Real Estate
sources.quote: calculated by dividing the monthly rent by the monthly principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and association dues (PITIA).

posts.text:
A lender gets an appraisal in January. The loan closes in August. Is that value still good?

It varies by lender. For loans sold to Fannie Mae, the Selling Guide calls for an appraisal update when an appraisal is more than four months old but under 12 months. If the update shows a decline, a new appraisal is required. Federal bank guidelines list passage of time and local market volatility as reasons a new appraisal may be necessary.

Illustrative: $425,000 falling 5 percent becomes $403,750.

Lenders can set an age limit and ask for an update.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Light graphic titled How old is too old for an appraisal. A bar shows 0 to 4 months, 4 to 12 months with an update, and over 12 months under the Fannie Mae benchmark. Illustrative cards: a $425,000 value falls 5 percent to $403,750, a $21,250 gap.

sources.title: B4-1.2-04, Appraisal Age and Use Requirements (06/04/2025)
sources.quote: When the effective date of the original appraisal report is more than four months but less than 12 months, the appraiser must perform an appraisal update that includes inspecting the exterior of the property. If the appraiser indicates on the Form 1004D that the property value has declined, then the lender must obtain a new appraisal for the property. When an appraisal is obtained, the property must be appraised within the 12 months prior to the date of the note and mortgage.

Such criteria will vary depending upon the condition of the property and the marketplace, and the nature of the transaction.

posts.text:
A 12 month bridge loan ends with a payoff. Can the permanent loan cover it?

Lenders can test the takeout first. Value: One source says a low appraisal reduces a DSCR loan, capped at 75 percent of appraised value. A hypothetical $430,000 appraisal gives $322,500. A $335,000 payoff leaves a $12,500 gap.

Coverage: DSCR is gross monthly rent divided by monthly PITIA. $2,650 over $2,850 is 0.93. One source says most DSCR lenders require at least 1.00.

Lease: One source says a month to month tenant or family member lease does not satisfy most DSCR lenders.

Cutoffs vary.

Annual tax returns
Insurance renewal proof before expiry

A named document and a date make a request checkable. Terms vary by lender.

posts.text:
A private loan is sold or its servicing moves. What must the borrower be told?

For covered consumer mortgage loans, Regulation X usually requires the outgoing servicer to give notice at least 15 days before a servicing transfer. The new servicer gives its own within 15 days after. Truth in Lending separately requires a new owner to notify the borrower within 30 days of a sale.

Regulation X exempts business purpose loans, and Truth in Lending generally does too. State rules vary.

Confirm loan purpose first, then check state law and the note with counsel. Not legal advice.
posts.alt: Timeline graphic of servicing transfer notices: the outgoing servicer notice at least 15 days before transfer, the new servicer notice within 15 days after, and a new owner notice within 30 days of a sale. A card notes business purpose loans are exempt from Regulation X.

sources.quote: not less than 15 days before the effective date of the transfer

sources.title: 12 CFR 1024.33 Mortgage servicing transfers
sources.quote: The transferee servicer shall provide the notice of transfer to the borrower not more than 15 days after the effective date of the transfer.

sources.title: 12 CFR 1024.5 Coverage of RESPA
sources.quote: (2) Business purpose loans. An extension of credit primarily for a business, commercial, or agricultural purpose, as defined by 12 CFR 1026.3(a)(1) of Regulation Z.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code 1641 Liability of assignees
sources.quote: not later than 30 days after the date on which a mortgage loan is sold or otherwise transferred or assigned to a third party, the creditor that is the new owner or assignee of the debt shall notify the borrower in writing of such transfer

posts.text:
A hypothetical $540,000 interest-only loan is priced at prime plus 4 percent, with an 11.5 percent floor. What happens if prime falls?

A rate floor limits how low an adjustable rate can drop. Illustrative primes:

Prime 7.75 percent: rate 11.75 percent.
Prime 6.75 percent: formula 10.75, floor sets 11.5 percent.
Prime 5.75 percent: formula 9.75, floor sets 11.5 percent.

At 11.5 percent, monthly interest is $5,175.00. At the 9.75 percent formula rate it would be $4,387.50. The floor keeps interest $787.50 a month above the formula rate.

Lenders can confirm whether a note has a floor.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Table of an illustrative $540,000 interest-only loan priced at prime plus 4 percent with an 11.5 percent floor. Prime 7.75 gives 11.75 percent; prime 6.75 and 5.75 give 11.50 percent because the floor applies. Monthly interest is $5,175.00 at the floor versus $4,387.50 at 9.75 percent.

sources.quote: An interest rate floor is the lowest interest rate that your adjustable-rate mortgage can have once its rate begins to adjust. A rate floor places a limit on how low the loan’s rate can drop.

sources.quote: An interest rate floor is the minimum interest rate possible for anadjustable rate mortgage.

posts.text:
Where is the original signed note right now?

The note is the borrower's written promise to repay. If a lender loses a note it was entitled to enforce, UCC 3-309 may let it enforce anyway, but it must prove the note's terms and its right to enforce. The court must also find the borrower is adequately protected against a claim by someone else.

In North Carolina, a lost note affidavit can attest to the loss and the terms. Rules vary by state.

Lenders can log where each original is held.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Three step cards from UCC 3-309 on what a lender without the original note must show: it was entitled to enforce when possession was lost, the loss was not a transfer or lawful seizure, and the note cannot be recovered. It must then prove the note terms and right to enforce.

sources.title: UCC 3-309. Enforcement of lost, destroyed, or stolen instrument
sources.publisher: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute
sources.quote: A person seeking enforcement of an instrument under subsection (a) must prove the terms of the instrument and the person's right to enforce the instrument. The court may not enter judgment in favor of the person seeking enforcement unless it finds that the person required to pay the instrument is adequately protected against loss that might occur by reason of a claim by another person to enforce the instrument.

posts.text:
A borrower stops paying. Payoff is $255,000. A buyer offers $215,000. Does the lender say yes?

That is a short sale: the lender agrees to a sale below the loan balance. The shortfall here is $40,000. Whether the borrower still owes it varies by state and by the lender agreement.

The alternative is foreclosure. A Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia paper found short sales sold for 9.2 to 10.5 percent more on average, and notes longer foreclosure timelines can raise lender costs.

Lenders can weigh the offer against the full cost and time of foreclosing.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Bar chart of an illustrative short sale: a $255,000 loan payoff versus a $215,000 buyer offer, leaving a $40,000 shortfall. Two cards compare a short sale, which needs lender approval, with foreclosure, which may add carrying costs.

sources.quote: A short sale, which is a type of loss mitigation, is a sale of your home for less than what you owe on your mortgage.

sources.title: What Is a Short Sale and How Does It Work?
sources.quote: A short sale occurs when a homeowner sells their home for an amount less than the full amount owed on the mortgage. The process can only begin with the approval of your mortgage lender. You may be required to pay the difference between that price and the remaining balance on your mortgage.

sources.title: A Shortage of Short Sales: Explaining the Underutilization of a Foreclosure Alternative (WP 19-13)
sources.quote: homes selling as short sales transact at 9.2% to 10.5% higher prices on average than those that sell after foreclosure. Longer foreclosure timelines increase costs for lenders because they may have to cover missed property taxes, hazard insurance, and homeowner association payments.

posts.text:
Does a 550 credit score end a hard money deal?

Not automatically. NerdWallet, on hard money business loans, says requirements are "largely based on the value of your collateral" and that lenders do not typically weigh credit score as heavily. Point says the biggest factor is not credit score but skin in the game, and that some lenders prefer a FICO of 550 or higher.

For rehab loans, Point adds that lenders often require a certain level of experience.

A lender can decide how much collateral, equity, experience and credit each count. That mix varies by lender.

vaultedonline.com
posts.alt: Four cards on what hard money guides say lenders weigh: collateral value, skin in the game, experience on rehab loans, and credit score, where a FICO of 550 or higher is preferred by some lenders. Weights vary by lender.

sources.title: Hard Money Business Loans: What They Are and When to Get One
sources.quote: Hard money business loan requirements are largely based on the value of your collateral. ... they don't typically weigh these factors as heavily when underwriting your application.

sources.title: Hard Money Loan Requirements
sources.quote: When it comes to qualifying for a hard money loan, the biggest factor isn't your credit score — it's your skin in the game. The minimum credit score is usually flexible, but a FICO score of 550 or higher is preferred by some lenders. Hard money lenders often require a certain level of experience if the intended use is to rehab distressed properties.

posts.text:
A title policy covers what it says, and an endorsement changes that. It is an addition to or limitation of coverage attached to the policy.

Three add-ons a lender can ask about:

Survey: covers a difference between the insured land and a survey. It generally needs an ALTA survey.

Access: without it, a policy does not insure a particular means of access.

Comprehensive: can cover items like restriction violations and encroachments, depending on the version.

Availability and wording vary by state and title company. Lenders can ask the title company which endorsements fit the property.

ALTA 25 endorsements provide coverage for loss or damage due to a difference in the land insured in the policy. ALTA 9 is an endorsement that provides coverage for unrecorded covenants, notices, encroachments, or setbacks at the property.

posts.text:
A lender takes back a property at foreclosure. Now the lender owns the bills.

Federal Reserve guidance for banks on foreclosed property lists property taxes, insurance, utilities kept at a level that preserves the property, and maintenance. FDIC guidance says taxes should be paid in a timely manner to avoid penalties and interest.

Illustrative monthly costs: taxes $540, insurance $310, utilities $180, upkeep $150. That is $1,180 a month, or $7,080 over six months.

Lenders can add holding costs to the resale timeline and price.

(page undated, accessed 2026-11-22; FAQ dated June 28, 2012). Also: Operating expenses include, but are not limited to, legal fees and direct costs incurred for foreclosure, property maintenance, and state and local government assessments.

posts.text:
A borrower misses a payment. Can the lender start remedies right away? Notice and cure requirements may apply first.

A notice of default is a formal written statement that a borrower has not met an obligation. It warns that remedies may follow if the default is not cured.

The cure period is the window to fix it. Illustrative: 15 days to pay the missed amount. Pay inside it and the default may be cured. Miss it, and remedies may follow.

Cure periods vary by transaction and loan documents, and state law may matter. Counsel can review both first.

posts.text:
Three terms that sound alike are different things.

A lien search looks for claims against a property. A title search reviews public records to confirm the legal owner and identify issues. A title commitment is a promise that the title insurance policy will be issued at closing.

One gap to know about: a traditional title search finds recorded liens only. A municipal lien search can find unrecorded items such as code violations and special assessments.

Lenders can ask the title company what was searched, and whether a municipal lien search fits the deal. Scope varies by state and lender.

posts.text:
A lender holds 24 loans. Six mature within 90 days. Would a year-end review catch them?

NCUA examiner guidance for credit unions says systems should "identify and report maturing loans," and that a lender should contact the borrower before maturity. It also lists paid property taxes. Abrigo lists insurance renewal due dates among items to track.

A year-end list:

1. Maturities in the next 90 days: 6 of 24 here
2. Insurance expirations
3. Property tax status
4. Late payers
5. Extension requests

Starting in December may leave time to call borrowers first. Process varies by lender.
